text:
mikaela: Heads-up: after the RBAC refactor rollout this morning we're seeing ~30 users JIT-provisioned as 'guest' instead of their expected org roles. Seems correlated with SSO assertions where primaryEmail is empty and alternateEmail is present. :rotating_light:
andre: Can you paste an example SAML assertion (sanitized)?
mikaela: sure, pasted minimal example below (sanitized):
```xml
<saml:Attribute Name="urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3">
  <saml:AttributeValue xsi:type="xs:string">
    <!-- primaryEmail missing -->
  </saml:AttributeValue>
</saml:Attribute>
<saml:Attribute Name="urn:oid:1.3.6.1.4.1.5923.1.1.1.9">
  <saml:AttributeValue>alt.email+okta@example.com</saml:AttributeValue>
</saml:Attribute>
```
laura: Repro notes? Is JIT using email as the canonical id now (we changed to prefer mail over sub last week)?
mikaela: Yes — the refactor made a change to prefer primaryEmail -> mail -> sub for identifier. If primaryEmail is present but empty we treat as missing and skip fallback to mail. Looks like Okta sometimes emits an empty element rather than omitting the attribute.
simon: That explains it. Empty string equals present in our parser today. We should trim and treat empty as absent. Quick patch possible?
andre: +1. Two things to consider: 1) patch parser to treat empty/whitespace-only attributes as absent; 2) migration for the ~30 users whose role was dropped. Do we have audit logs tying the JIT event to the SAML assertion and KMS-decrypted blob?
sec-oncall-bot: Incident recorded: SEC-2026-104. Affected users: 31. Initial triage assigned to @andre and @mikaela. :clipboard:
ashley: For rollback/migration: can we re-run the JIT mapping job for those users without triggering full reprovision? I can run a one-off reconciliation if we can fetch the original assertion or reconstruct attributes from Okta API.
mikaela: Okta's API shows the alternateEmail on the user object. The SAML assertion was not persisted in plaintext by default — we log assertion HMAC and an encrypted payload stored via KMS. Question: do we have the decrypted assertion for these events or do we need to call the Key Decrypt API for each?
andre: We store the encrypted assertion blob in audit_logs.encrypted_assertion along with kms_key_id and ciphertext_checksum. We can call internal KMS service to decrypt for each audit row, but need approval from security to access PII.
laura: We should avoid decrypting unless necessary. Option A: Re-run mapping using Okta user API (no SAML payload) to reassign roles. Option B: Decrypt assertions but redact PII before writing anywhere. Which is faster?
simon: Re-run mapping is faster and safer. We'll get the same attributes from Okta for these users. I can script a job: fetch user list from SEC-2026-104, call internal mapping codepath with current Okta attributes, push role update events.
ashley: If mapping job uses the same code as production refactor path it will hit the same bug. We should run it against the patched mapper worker (treat empty as absent) and only after unit tests.
mikaela: I tested the patch locally: two-line change in saml_parser.trim_attribute() -> return None for empty. Unit tests added. Patch ready for canary.
andré: (typo) Andre: SGTM. Let's canary on staging, then opt-in 10% of prod traffic, monitor token-level audit. Can @mike help with the rollout/console flags?
mike: I can expose a feature flag (rbac.saml_empty_attr_fallback=true) in Console by EOD. Will wire dashboard metrics for JIT failures and roles_changed_count.
andre: Also: we need an audit trail entry for the 31 reconciled accounts: create a migration job that emits audit_log entries with reason="sso_empty_attr_reconcile" and actor="system:reconcile_bot". Ensure no PII in the audit payload.
laura: KMS question: if we do need to decrypt an assertion, who signs off? @sec-oncall-bot I assume primary approval chain is security lead + privacy.
sec-oncall-bot: Approval required: security_lead + privacy_officer. Request ticket created: SEC-2026-104-decrypt.
mikaela: For transparency, I've attached repro steps and a test assertion to the ticket.
simon: Plan: 1) patch saml parser, 2) run unit/integration tests, 3) deploy canary flag at 10%, 4) reconcile affected users using patched mapper (no decryption), 5) monitor metrics, 6) expand rollout.
andré: timeline?
mikaela: Patch PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/saml-parser/pulls/42. If we merge today we can canary tonight and run reconcile tomorrow morning.
mike: Flag deployed on staging, metric hooks live.
ashley: I'll prep the reconciliation job and hold until canary green.
laura: Also add an alert if Okta starts sending empty attributes more than 0.1% of assertions — could indicate upstream change.
mikaela: Good call. I'll add that alert to the SSO ingest monitor.
andre: Thanks everyone. Postmortem notes: root cause = parser treated empty attribute as present; mitigation = parser fix + reconciliation; follow-up = alert and guidance to Okta admins to omit empty attributes. :white_check_mark:
